evidence: This term originates from the feudal period in Vietnam, where it was used to denote four key officials who were considered the pillars of the royal court, particularly during the dynasties of the Đinh and Nguyễn periods. Currently, the term 'The four pillars' is primarily used by public opinion, some media outlets, independent analysts, and non-official voices in Vietnam.

These four officials were revered by later generations as the 'Four Pillars' of the court. In the Tràng An World Heritage Site, there is a temple dedicated to these four great officials, known as the Temple of the Four Pillars.
